chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar and others, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, by a chain he mentioned, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man enters a city, he is a guest upon those in it from the people of his religion, until he departs from them. And it is not befitting for the guest that he should fast except with their permission, lest they prepare something which would spoil for them. And it is not befitting for them that they should fast except with the permission of the guest, lest he be shy of them, so he would desire the food but leave it for them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a traveler fasting while visiting locals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the reciprocal rights between host and guest, emphasizing that voluntary fasting by either party can disrupt the communal dining experience and cause social discomfort (ikhtisham). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining harmony and preventing hardship (darar) within the community during shared meals, ensuring that individual acts of worship do not become a source of inconvenience for others.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar and someone else, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, by a chain he mentioned, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When a man enters a city, so he is a guest upon the ones who are in it, from the people of his Religion, until he departs from them. And, it is not befitting for the guest that he should be Fasting except with their permission, perhaps they would be making something, so it would spoil upon them. And, it is not befitting for them that they should be Fasting except with the permission of the guest, perhaps he would be embarrassed, so he would desire the food, but he would leave it for them’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar [and others] from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq through his chain of narrators from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith: ‘

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “When a man enters a town (residence), he is a guest of the inhabitants of that town who are followers of the religion he follows until he leaves that town (residence). It is not proper for him to fast without their permission, so that the food that may have been prepared does not spoil. It is not proper for them also to fast without permission so he because of exercising reservation does not eat the food that he desires.’””
